segments: And when they took Amid,
they desired also to go against Mayperqat and subdue it.
Now al-Malik al-Ghazi, its lord,
the brother of al-Kamil,
sent and brought Khwarazmians from Mesopotamia to his aid.
And he was strengthened, and was not defeated by his enemies,
especially since the people of Aleppo held back from the war with him,
because he was the brother of their mistress,
that is to say, of the mother of al-Malik al-Zahir, the father of al-Malik al-Nasir, lord of Aleppo.
Now Sinan, when he had taken Amid,
received an order from the Sultan to go to Erzurum,
and to rule there and stand against the onslaught of the Tatars.
And as soon as he went,
Chormaqan Noyan came with a powerful force of the Tatars.
And in a few days they captured that fortress,
and put all its population, men and women, to the edge of the sword,
except for boys and girls who were suitable for slavery.
And Sinan himself and his young son they likewise killed,
and they left it desolate and departed.
And at the turn of the year,
which was the year 1553 [AG],
the Tatars came out again and reached as far as the territory of Hisn Ziyad {OCR?},
and plundered everything they found,
and returned to Persia.
And in the year 1554,
horsemen for gold from Aleppo, and from the Greeks, and from the Franks, and from the Ma'addites {Arabs}.
Now the lord of Homs and al-Malik al-Ghazi the lord of Mayperqat promised that they too would come,
but they acted deceitfully towards the Sultan and did not come.
And Baron Constantine, the father of Hetoum, king of the Armenians, came to the Sultan in Caesarea,
and was received with great honor,
and he received {OCR?} many gifts,
and promised that he would go and gather an army of Armenians and come to the aid of the Sultan.
And the Sultan himself marched toward Sebastia.
And the Tatars also came and entered the territory of Erzincan.
And the Sultan hastened and went out against them,
and his forces met the Tatars at a place called Köse Dağ,
that is to say, the Bald Mountain.
And like inexperienced men,
from the very beginning of the clash they turned their backs,
and were utterly unable to endure before the Tatars;
rather, in a single hour they fled,
and left the Sultan all alone.
